description: Disabling padding can expose the inherited activation kernel's missing odd-element tail.
trigger: A direct GatedMLP caller selects pad_to=1 and runs FP16 projections with an odd total intermediate element count, for example one token, hidden_size=128 and intermediate_size=129.
expected_behavior: Every intermediate element becomes activation(gate) multiplied by up before the down projection.
actual_behavior: act_mul_kernel processes only numel // 2 half2 pairs. With 129 elements, the last up element remains ungated and is consumed by down. No even-element guard is added. The inspected model constructors retain padding, so this observation concerns opt-in callers rather than all existing model workflows.

finding.description: The inherited activation kernels still leave an odd final element unwritten; the new separate destination does not repair that boundary.
finding.trigger: Execute GatedMLP with an otherwise valid unpadded intermediate whose total element count is odd, or directly call either activation wrapper with odd-length buffers.
finding.expected_behavior: Every activation destination element receives activation(g) × u.
finding.actual_behavior: Both kernels process only complete pairs. With separate a storage the final element is unwritten; with in-place u it retains the ungated up value. Default padding normally avoids odd widths, so this is not evidence of failure for ordinary padded models.
